head: 9e13b0920632d8707c0622f67c53b0a8e513c98a
summary: SL-065 replaced the outcome panel's trigger-driven star rows with OutcomeTexts above one TabControl (OutcomeTabs: Largest files, Unreadable folders (N)), a generic EnsureSelectedTabIsVisible() guard, additive schema-1 report keys with an UnreadableExpander alias, and a structural rule against a ScrollViewer directly around a list. The layout half passed in one build, and all 12 window cases passed on a real desktop (S-001..S-009, B-007, B-008, C-001). The remaining rework (builds 2-3, code-reviews 3-6, validates 2-6) was all one regex, `.taad/fitness.yaml:810`, the ScrollViewer rule, which was rewritten three times. It was accepted at 9e13b09 with O-018 (in-comment false positive, two XML-legal false negatives) still open in the record.

payload.summary: SL-065 replaced the outcome panel's trigger-driven star rows with OutcomeTexts above one TabControl (OutcomeTabs: Largest files, Unreadable folders (N)), a generic EnsureSelectedTabIsVisible() guard, additive schema-1 report keys with an UnreadableExpander alias, and a structural rule against a ScrollViewer directly around a list. The layout half passed in one build, and all 12 window cases passed on a real desktop (S-001..S-009, B-007, B-008, C-001). The remaining rework (builds 2-3, code-reviews 3-6, validates 2-6) was all one regex, `.taad/fitness.yaml:810`, the ScrollViewer rule, which was rewritten three times. It was accepted at 9e13b09 with O-018 (in-comment false positive, two XML-legal false negatives) still open in the record.
payload.estimate_error: Opened as medium, low risk, one designer, sized by a person. The layout work was sized about right. Build-check cut two of the four criteria as already met, because SL-047 had raised MinHeight to 644 and made the Validate #3 repro unreachable, and the tab restructure then went through build, review and validate-1 with no layout rework. The risk tier was wrong. The design added an architecture rule, a multi-line must_not_match over MainWindow.xaml plus plant rows, after the slice was sized. That rule caused every send-back: 2 of 3 builds, 4 of 6 code-reviews and 5 of 6 validates. At 'low' the critique and critique-review were skipped, so the rule's regex was first attacked at code review. The skip saved little, since the same slice then needed 6 code-reviews and 6 validates.
what_went_wrong: One regex consumed most of the slice. The pattern at .taad/fitness.yaml:810 was replaced three times (O-016, O-017, O-018). The record shows builds 2-3, code-reviews 3-6 and validates 2-6 driven by it, against one clean pass for the actual tab layout.

The first review's replacement pattern (accepted for O-016) used unbounded lazy `.*?` spans under (?s). It fired on legitimate XAML: a comment as DriveScroller's first child (line 114) or after `</ScrollViewer.Style>` (289). The reviewer's own check, 'quiet on the clean tree', could not see that, because the clean tree has no comment in those spots. Two more rounds were needed.

The tempered-token fix (build 3) left the rule with known defects. It still fires on ScrollViewer+list text inside an XML comment, misses `</ScrollViewer.Style >` with a space, and misses a self-closing `<ScrollViewer.Resources />` before a list. Validate-5 measured all four at HEAD. O-018 was still open at reflect and the record shows no person's decision on it. A fourth pattern is now proposed, on a rule that has been wrong three times.

eng/rules-harness/harness.py never ran end to end in any of the three builds. It exits 2 (CANNOT MEASURE) on the pre-existing UNRAN must_not_import rule 'the provider does not use the code it checks'. Every revision of the regex, S09-S13 and the '35 rows' claim rests on ad-hoc probes of taad3.fitness that skip check_clean. The design named the plant row as the proof that the rule fires, without checking that the harness could measure.

The critique and critique-review were skipped by the low-risk sizing. The design's `(?s)<ScrollViewer\b[^>]*>\s*<(ListView|...)` allowed only whitespace between the tags. MainWindow.xaml puts an XML comment above almost every element and opens OutcomeTexts with a `<ScrollViewer.Style>` property element (lines 289-299). A five-minute read of the file would have shown the house style slips through.

Validate-3 and validate-5 republished the exe and re-ran all 12 window cases for changes confined to fitness.yaml and plants.json. Build 3 had already said, correctly, that neither file is in the exe. The desktop evidence was redundant. The rule evidence was the part that needed re-measuring.

Build-check ran B-007 and C-001 in a sandbox with no interactive window station. Both timed out, along with the trivial --report run, and produced no usable signal. Only validate has a desktop, so every build-stage and review-stage claim about window layout was structural.

missed.what: The design's must_not_match allowed only whitespace between `<ScrollViewer ...>` and the list. It was never checked against MainWindow.xaml's house style: a `<!-- -->` comment above almost every element, and `<ScrollViewer.Style>` property elements (OutcomeTexts, lines 289-299). A new section written in the house style would have passed the rule, and the regression it guards (100,001 containers, 229.7 s, about 2 GB) would have passed every gate. The critique did not run at all (low tier), so nothing asked what the rule does on the lines it was written for.
missed.caught_by: code-review (R2-M1, first pass), then confirmed by validate-2 sending the slice back

missed.what: The design made the plant-row harness the proof that the rule fires on multi-line XAML. Nobody asked whether eng/rules-harness/harness.py can measure at this HEAD. It exits 2 (CANNOT MEASURE) because of the pre-existing UNRAN import rule 'the provider does not use the code it checks'. So the plant rows S09-S13 were never run by the harness across three builds.
missed.caught_by: build-slice (attempt 1 hit exit 2, and attempts 2-3 hit the same cause)

missed.what: The pattern the first review prescribed for R2-M1 had unbounded lazy `<!--.*?-->` and `.*?</ScrollViewer\.\1>` spans under (?s), so they extend past the first closing token to a later one anywhere in the file. The review's 'quiet on clean tree (OutcomeTexts and DriveScroller included)' evidence did not include a comment placed inside those elements. MainWindow.xaml already has a comment ending at 443 directly above `<TreeView x:Name="FolderTree"`, and the pattern fired at 114 and 289 on legitimate XAML.
missed.caught_by: code-review (incremental re-read, second R2-M1), then validate-3/4, which sent the slice back to build a second time

missed.what: The second review's tempered-token pattern was passed on 'nothing I tried produced a false positive'. It did not test text inside an XML comment, although .taad/fitness.yaml:57-60 says the engine blanks only // and /* */ and not `<!-- -->` for .xaml. The likeliest place for that text is the tag-form example in the MainWindow.xaml:178-190 contract comment that later section slices are meant to extend. It also left `</ScrollViewer.Style >` and self-closing `<ScrollViewer.Resources />` as false negatives.
missed.caught_by: code-review (attempt 5, M1), then measured at HEAD by validate-5 (fires at 190 and 363, two hits beside one real violation)

learned.lesson: Re-tier a slice when its design adds a must_not_match rule over XAML. The layout change here was low risk. The regex guard was not, and it caused nearly all the rework. At 'low' the critique and critique-review did not run, and the guard was first attacked by code review, one round at a time.
learned.evidence: Build 1 passed layout review and validate-1 on all 12 cases. Builds 2-3, code-reviews 3-6 and validates 2-6 were all fitness.yaml:810. The critique and critique-review were 'none contact' (skipped by sizing).

learned.lesson: For .xaml, the fitness engine blanks only // and /* */ comments, not `<!-- -->`, so any must_not_match over MainWindow.xaml matches comment text. Write and measure every XAML rule against the file's house style: a comment above almost every element, `<X.Style>` property elements, a comment as the first child of DriveScroller (line 114), a comment after `</ScrollViewer.Style>` (289), and a tag-form example inside the contract comment (178-190).
learned.evidence: fitness.yaml:57-60. O-016/O-017/O-018 were each a shape from that list that the previous pattern got wrong. Validate-5 measured O-018 firing at 190 and 363.

learned.lesson: Build one fire/quiet corpus for a rule before writing its pattern, and put it in plants.json. Validate-5 already has an 18-variant corpus, and O-018's proposed pattern scored 18/18 on it. Do not grow the shapes one review round at a time. Each round verified only the shapes its reviewer thought of, and the next round found the next one.
learned.evidence: S09-S13 were added across three builds. Each pattern passed its own reviewer's measurements and failed the next round's shape. Round 1 missed comments and property elements, round 2 fired on legitimate comments, and round 3 left in-comment text and two XML-legal false negatives.

learned.lesson: eng/rules-harness/harness.py cannot measure at this HEAD, and any slice that relies on plant-row proof is unverified until that is fixed. It exits 2 because the must_not_import rule 'the provider does not use the code it checks' comes back UNRAN and check_clean refuses the baseline. Build-check should run the harness before a design leans on plant rows. Attempt 2 found that fitness.check(tree, build=True) alone does not fix it, because the scratch copy lacks a .git or .code-review-graph marker.
learned.evidence: Exit 2 in build attempts 1-3 and in validate-3 and validate-5. The 35-row plants.json (19+3+8+5) was measured only through Planting/judge/run_xunit called directly, bypassing check_clean.

learned.lesson: The tab contract the next section slices inherit is one section = one TabItem in OutcomeTabs. Add no RowDefinition, MinHeight, DataTrigger, ScrollViewer, StackPanel or Auto row around a list. Call EnsureSelectedTabIsVisible() after any visibility change, keep OutcomeTabs.stripRows==1, and add report keys in the flat named style. Keep emitting the UnreadableExpander alias. Four headers ('Largest files', 'Largest folders', 'By extension', 'Unreadable folders (12,345)') fit one strip row at 560 in a scratch build (O-002/O-003). No real third section has been rendered, and no tab whose content is a Grid with an Auto caption plus a * list has been exercised.
learned.evidence: S-007 (stripRows 1 at 12,345). The design's 'rule for adding an analysis section' contract. Validate-5 'not reached': real Largest folders and By extension sections. Its third-TabItem shapes were written only for the rule probe.

learned.lesson: Do not put a ScrollViewer around a list or tree in MainWindow. Spike 1 measured a ScrollViewer host realizing 100,001 containers (tree expand 229.7 s, about 2 GB) unless each list has a fixed Height. A TabControl in a star row kept it to 76 tree and 37 list containers at 165.6 ms. The observable proxy is a list's actualHeight <= OutcomeTabs.actualHeight. Rerun it for every new section (S-008, floor and maximized).
learned.evidence: Risk spike constraints 1-3 and S-008 (tabs grow 187 to 491 px maximized, and full rows go from 1 to 21).

learned.lesson: Window cases (WindowCases.ps1 B-007/B-008/C-001/S-00x) only produce signal on an interactive desktop, and only validate has one. Every case timed out in the build-check sandbox, including C-001 and a bare --report run. Report 'not run' from build and code-review, and use validate for layout evidence. When only fitness.yaml or plants.json changed, validate should re-measure the rule and not republish the exe and rerun the window suite.
learned.evidence: Build-check exit 1, actual TIMEOUT on B-007 and C-001, and the exe hung for 30 s. Build 3 said 'neither is in the exe'. Validate-5 still republished and re-ran all 12 cases.

learned.lesson: Before opening a slice from a reflection candidate, check `git log` on the target file since the reflection. This slice came from SL-040's reflection, and SL-047 had already raised MinHeight 600 to 644, which made the 880x560 and 560x400 repro unreachable. Build-check cut two of the four criteria, and the slice's real remaining work was the tab restructure.
learned.evidence: Build-check: no MainWindow.xaml commit since SL-047 (418cc8e). Window.MinHeight 644 at MainWindow.xaml:5, and the comment at 143-172 (before the rewrite) derives the fit.

candidates.title: Make eng/rules-harness/harness.py able to measure: give the scratch copy a root marker, or make check_clean tolerate the UNRAN must_not_import rule 'the provider does not use the code it checks'
candidates.why: It exits 2 (CANNOT MEASURE) at this HEAD. Three builds and validate-3/5 could check the SL-065 rule and rows S09-S13 only through ad-hoc probes. Nothing catches a fourth regression of the rule, or a bad plant row in any later rule slice.

candidates.title: Close O-018: replace the ScrollViewer rule's pattern with the reviewer's in-comment-guarded pattern, and pin the whole 18-variant corpus in plants.json
candidates.why: At HEAD the rule fires on ScrollViewer+list text inside an XML comment (190, 363) and gives two hits beside one real violation. It misses `</ScrollViewer.Style >` and a self-closing `<ScrollViewer.Resources />` before a list. Check first whether a person deferred it. The third-section slice is likely to comment the contract block at MainWindow.xaml:178-190. Add a quiet row for a comment inside DriveScroller and rows for both false negatives, so the fourth pattern is measured against the fixed corpus and not a new round of guesses.

candidates.title: Run the person-run network pass (N-001..N-004, StalledShareTests) and a whole-drive C:\ scan ending at the floor and maximized, against the tab layout
candidates.why: Validate-5 did not reach them. The network pass is opt-in and this slice's MainWindow and hook changes made it stale. The real-folder runs (C:\Program Files, C:\ProgramData) rest on validate-1 at f513faf, and a C:\ ending was never run with the tabs.

unknowns: Was O-018 deferred by a person or left open when validate-6 accepted 9e13b09? The record shows it open, and validate-5 measured it real at HEAD. If it was not deferred, the slice shipped with a rule whose known defects contradict the rule's own 'because'.

Does the person want two analysis sections visible at once, such as Largest files beside By extension? Tabs preclude it. If yes, the next slices need a splitter or a second tab host, and the 'one section = one TabItem' contract changes. This is still unanswered from the design.

Does a tab whose content is a Grid (Auto caption row + * list row) keep the list bounded and keep OutcomeTabs.stripRows==1 with real content? The design allows that shape for later sections, but validate only rendered two real tabs. The other shapes were written for the rule probe.
Will a fourth rewrite of the pattern at fitness.yaml:810 hold? The 18-variant corpus is measured only on scratch copies through taad3.fitness, and nothing has run it end to end through the harness.
